newsitem.title: USA: Cultists thought they'd exit on "clouds of light".
newsitem.headline: Cultists thought they'd exit on "clouds of light".

text.p: A leaflet distributed by Heaven's Gate cult founder Marshall Applewhite's followers told recruits they would leave Earth on a spacecraft or on "clouds of light", according to a copy uncovered on Friday.
The promotional flier distributed to the news media during a 1994 recruiting drive in Maine and New Hampshire carried the headline "UFOs, SPACE ALIENS, AND THEIR FINAL FIGHT FOR EARTH'S SPOILS."

The leaflet said the offer to join an "exiting" of the Earth and "human-mammalian" bodies was being made "for the third and last time in this civilisation," but there is no direct reference to suicide.

"The two representatives who came in the early 1970's, and their crew -- student reps -- all came and will leave in spacecrafts or 'clouds of light' -- the same way the representatives left 2000 years ago," according to the flier.
The "two representatives" are referred to in the document as "Te and Do." Authorites have identified Do as Applewhite, who was one of the 39 people killed in this week's mass suicide in California.

The leaflet did not list the group's name and the room at the Portland Public Library for the August 11, 1994, recruiting session was reserved by "Total Overcomers Anonymous" -- a name which other reports have linked to Applewhite's organisation.

The leaflet describes Te and Do as "older members of the Kingdom of Heaven" who returned to Earth in 1975 in search of people willing to give up control of their bodies so their souls can prepared to travel to "An Evolutionary Kingdom Level Above Human."
"It is that loyalty and personal relationship with that Older Member that motivates those behavioural changes and makes the 'newborn' viable," the leaflet read.
The neatly handwritten flier draws a direct comparison between Do and Jesus, declaring that Do has the "same relationship with his crew" as "Jesus was in with his disciples."

"If this strikes a 'chord' in you, you have received a 'chip' -- of recognition -- from the Next Level -- though the hard work of changeover' can only be done by your unending effort under the supervision of the reps here now," the flier continued.
The leaflet implied there was some competition between members of the "Higher Kingdom" for humans, charging that "adversary forces" have "corrupted" all other religions.
